title: Global sections of a resolution of the direct image of injectives is a quasi-isomorphism
statement: Let $h:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let $\mathcal I^\bullet$ be a cochain complex of injective $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-sp-injective-resolutions], [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] with $\mathcal I^n=0$ for $n<0$, and $h_*\mathcal I^\bullet$ the complex of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules obtained by applying the direct image $h_*$ [def-pc-module-pullback] termwise, $(h_*\mathcal I^n)(V)=\mathcal I^n(h^{-1}V)$. Let $\mathcal J'^\bullet$ be a cochain complex of injective $\mathcal O_Y$-modules with $\mathcal J'^n=0$ for $n<0$ and $\lambda:h_*\mathcal I^\bullet\to\mathcal J'^\bullet$ a quasi-isomorphism [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules]. Then $\Gamma(Y,\lambda):\Gamma(Y,h_*\mathcal I^\bullet)=\Gamma(X,\mathcal I^\bullet)\to\Gamma(Y,\mathcal J'^\bullet)$ is a quasi-isomorphism of complexes of abelian groups (indeed of $\mathcal O_Y(Y)$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]): $H^p(\Gamma(Y,\lambda))$ is bijective for every $p$.

source.place: Cohomology of Sheaves, Remark 01FB (remark-explain-arrow: 'The vertical arrow is a quasi-isomorphism by Lemma 01EZ'), Lemma 01EZ (lemma-before-Leray) with Remark 01F0 (remark-elucidate-lemma), Lemma 01EX (lemma-pushforward-injective: $h_*\mathcal I$ is right acyclic for $\Gamma(V,-)$); literature/stacks-project/derived.tex Lemma 015E (lemma-leray-acyclicity)

proof.text: *Setting.* Put $\mathcal A=\Mod(\mathcal O_Y)$, the abelian category of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], $\mathcal B$ the abelian category of $\mathcal O_Y(Y)$-modules, and $F=\Gamma(Y,-):\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, $\mathcal G\mapsto\mathcal G(Y)$. $\mathcal A$ has enough injectives [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-modules-enough-injectives]. $F$ is additive, since the addition of morphisms of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules is computed on sections. $F$ preserves kernels: the kernel of $u:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G'$ is the limit of the diagram $(u,0):\mathcal G\rightrightarrows\mathcal G'$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise] evaluation at the open $Y$ carries that limit to the limit of the $\mathcal O_Y(Y)$-modules, i.e. $\Gamma(Y,\ker u)=\ker(u_Y)$. So $F$ is left exact additive [def-sp-left-exact-additive], its right derived functors computed by injective resolutions in $\Mod(\mathcal O_Y)$ are the cohomology groups $H^q(Y,-)$ [pqf-def-cohomology], and an $\mathcal O_Y$-module is $F$-acyclic [def-sp-acyclic] iff $H^q(Y,-)$ of it vanishes for all $q>0$.

source.place: Lemma 01EZ (lemma-before-Leray, line 2092), proof: the functor $\Gamma(Y,-)$ on $\mathcal O_Y$-modules with values in $\mathcal O_Y(Y)$-modules

proof.text: *$h_*\mathcal I^\bullet$ is a bounded-below complex of $\Gamma(Y,-)$-acyclic modules.* The direct image $h_*$ [def-pc-module-pullback] is an additive functor $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)\to\Mod(\mathcal O_Y)$ (on sections over $V$ it is the map on sections over $h^{-1}V$), so applied termwise to $\mathcal I^\bullet$ it gives a cochain complex $h_*\mathcal I^\bullet$ [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] with differentials $h_*(d^n)$, and $h_*\mathcal I^n=h_*0=0$ for $n<0$. For each $n$, $\mathcal I^n$ is an injective $\mathcal O_X$-module, so by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pushforward-injective-acyclic] (with $V=Y$) $H^q(Y,h_*\mathcal I^n)=0$ for all $q>0$: $h_*\mathcal I^n$ is $\Gamma(Y,-)$-acyclic [def-sp-acyclic] (Step 1).

source.place: Lemma 01EX (lemma-pushforward-injective, line 1779) (2), as used in the proof of Lemma 01EZ and in Remark 01F0

proof.text: *$\mathcal J'^\bullet$ is a bounded-below complex of $\Gamma(Y,-)$-acyclic modules.* $\mathcal J'^n=0$ for $n<0$, and each $\mathcal J'^n$ is an injective object of $\Mod(\mathcal O_Y)$, which has enough injectives (Step 1); by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-injective-vanishing] (for $v=\Gamma(Y,-)$) $R^q\Gamma(Y,\mathcal J'^n)=H^q(Y,\mathcal J'^n)=0$ for all $q>0$, i.e. $\mathcal J'^n$ is $\Gamma(Y,-)$-acyclic [def-sp-acyclic].

*Leray acyclicity.* $\lambda:h_*\mathcal I^\bullet\to\mathcal J'^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism of complexes of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules]: $H^r(\lambda)$ is an isomorphism of the cohomology objects of $\Mod(\mathcal O_Y)$ for every $r$, which is the notion of quasi-isomorphism of complexes of the abelian category $\mathcal A=\Mod(\mathcal O_Y)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity-quasi-iso] to $\mathcal A$, $\mathcal B$, $F=\Gamma(Y,-)$ (Step 1), $K^\bullet=h_*\mathcal I^\bullet$, $L^\bullet=\mathcal J'^\bullet$, $a=0$ (all terms $F$-acyclic by Steps 2 and 3) and $\varphi=\lambda$: the morphism $\Gamma(Y,\lambda):\Gamma(Y,h_*\mathcal I^\bullet)\to\Gamma(Y,\mathcal J'^\bullet)$, $\Gamma(Y,\lambda)^n=\lambda^n_Y$, is a quasi-isomorphism of complexes of $\mathcal O_Y(Y)$-modules.

source.place: Remark 01F0 (remark-elucidate-lemma, line 2147): '$R\Gamma(Y,Rf_*\mathcal F)$ is represented by $\Gamma(Y,f_*\mathcal I^\bullet)$ ... from Leray's acyclicity lemma (Derived Categories, Lemma 015E) and Lemma 01EX'; Remark 01FB (line 2391): 'the vertical arrow is a quasi-isomorphism'

proof.text: *Conclusion.* By the definition of the direct image, $\Gamma(Y,h_*\mathcal I^n)=(h_*\mathcal I^n)(Y)=\mathcal I^n(h^{-1}Y)=\mathcal I^n(X)=\Gamma(X,\mathcal I^n)$, with differential $(h_*d^n)_Y=d^n_X$ [def-pc-module-pullback], so $\Gamma(Y,h_*\mathcal I^\bullet)=\Gamma(X,\mathcal I^\bullet)$ as complexes, $\mathcal O_Y(Y)$ acting through $h^\sharp:\mathcal O_Y(Y)\to\mathcal O_X(X)$. Kernels, images and cokernels of $\mathcal O_Y(Y)$-linear maps are those of the underlying abelian groups, so $H^p$ of a complex of $\mathcal O_Y(Y)$-modules has as underlying group $H^p$ of the underlying complex of abelian groups, and an isomorphism of modules is bijective. By Step 4, $H^p(\Gamma(Y,\lambda)):H^p(\Gamma(X,\mathcal I^\bullet))\to H^p(\Gamma(Y,\mathcal J'^\bullet))$ is bijective for every $p$: $\Gamma(Y,\lambda)$ is a quasi-isomorphism of complexes of abelian groups and of $\mathcal O_Y(Y)$-modules.
